findings.suggested_fix: Guard each cleanup step, record its exception in failures, attempt all remaining cleanup, and set success and correct only after reset has succeeded; mark cleanup-incomplete manifests explicitly.
findings.title: Record cleanup failures before declaring a session successful
findings.why_it_matters: If session reset fails after grading, the finally block still writes a manifest reporting success and an empty failure list, and later slots accept that manifest as complete. Earlier cleanup errors can also skip service shutdown, firewall removal, and working-tree capture while still producing a manifest. Collect cleanup errors independently, continue the remaining cleanup, and only report success after cleanup succeeds so incomplete runs cannot look valid.
findings.validation_reason: If reset fails after a successful grade, the new harness sets success and correct before p4.reset, writes the manifest in its finally block, and reserve accepts its existence; Phase 4 reset can raise on surviving processes or files, though incidence was not measured.

Add controls for the pinned Codex bash -lc representation, bare commands, quoted absolute executable paths, and failed commands.
findings.title: Recognize shell-wrapped push commands
findings.why_it_matters: A successful Codex upgrade executed as /bin/bash -lc 'mo push main.mo ...' is graded as having no command-origin push. The quote immediately before mo fails the new regex, so proxy.match leaves its upload calls unmatched and grade.attestation cannot recognize the successful command either. The Phase4 pilot ledger explicitly records that this pinned Codex client wraps its commands in bash -lc, making the stub's bare-command coverage insufficient for the actual evaluation.

findings.suggested_fix: Catch TimeoutExpired and process launch failures, write available stdout and stderr and an attempt record with timeout or error details, and persist the record before parsing or validating reports.
findings.title: Record compiler attempts before handling timeouts or malformed output
findings.why_it_matters: A compiler timeout leaves no attempt record or captured output, and malformed JSON also prevents the attempt from being recorded. These are precisely the failures needed to investigate compiler-stall evidence; the retained input alone does not say how the attempt ended or preserve its diagnostics. Recording the outcome and raw streams before parsing preserves that evidence.
findings.validation_reason: If a compiler invocation times out or returns malformed JSON, the new compiler_load.py exits before appending and writing its attempt record, and timeout also precedes both output writes; incidence was not measured.

publish.py:4: publish.py SESSIONS_JSON DEST --tokens SERVICE_TOKENS PROVIDER_SECRETS
publish.py:190: parser.add_argument('--tokens', nargs='+', required=True). One file is accepted.
findings.first_evidence: learnability/phase5/evaluation/publish.py:118: if len({token for _, token in tokens}) < 2:
findings.suggested_fix: Take separate options (`--service-tokens` and `--provider-secrets`), require both files to be non-empty, and record both file digests in the receipt. At minimum, require exactly two files and at least one token from each.
findings.title: Publication accepts tokens without provider secrets, despite documenting both
findings.why_it_matters: The docstring requires SERVICE_TOKENS and PROVIDER_SECRETS, but the check only needs two distinct tokens in total. The harness's tokens file alone holds at least 8 per-session service tokens, so `--tokens STATE/tokens` passes without STATE/secrets. Provider OAuth or API secrets in stream.jsonl, client-stderr.txt or service.log are then neither redacted nor caught by the stage and extract scans, and the receipt says publication_scan_clean: true. One operator omission leaks credentials into the archive.
findings.validation_reason: If the operator supplies only the service-token file and a distinct provider secret occurs in a published artifact without matching its patterns, the new publisher accepts two service tokens, redacts and scans only supplied patterns, and reports a clean receipt; harness.py appends two fresh service tokens per session and incidence of such secret-bearing artifacts was not measured.

triage_groups.context: Both issues can turn successful sessions into misses.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Correct command recognition and tolerate documented client events, then exercise real transcript shapes.
triage_groups.why: Both paths feed the same protected grading result.

triage_groups.title: Failure evidence and cleanup
triage_groups.context: Exceptional paths can misreport cleanup or lose diagnostics.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Record each failure and attempt remaining cleanup, retaining partial command outputs.
triage_groups.why: The evidence must make failed measurements and incomplete sessions auditable.
